answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock a non-transferable reputation bond, an onyx stake, before it may transact. The bond is earned only through verified work, never bought, and slashed on fraud. A quill-signed work history accrues over time, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero trust and must pay the full cost of building history, while honest agents keep compounding theirs. Peer attestation adds shale layers that check work claims against real outputs, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand histories, not one copy-paste.
